results.title: Exa's Websets V2 Runs 4x Faster at Half the Cost for Web Research | AlphaSignal
results.content:
### Limits to budget for

- Variable spend: There is no fixed price per row. Complex criteria, extensive verification, and enrichment can increase ACU usage.
- Irreversible migration: Existing Starter and Pro customers retain their previous pricing until they opt in. After switching to usage-based billing, they cannot return to the old plan.
- Incomplete coverage: Higher recall still leaves gaps. Teams should test coverage before using a Webset as an exhaustive source.
- Data obligations: Citations help with review, while customers remain responsible for licensing, privacy, retention, and outreach requirements in their own applications.

## One asynchronous API job [...] - Exa released Websets V2: 4x faster dataset building at roughly half the cost per match.
- Accuracy and recall are up 20%, and the gains apply automatically for all users with no code changes.
- The subscription is gone; pricing is now $0.10 per compute unit plus $5 per 1,000 searches.
- Every usage-plan user gets API access, billed from the same credits as Exa's Search API.
- On Exa's own benchmarks, V2 averaged $0.017 to $0.024 per verified match versus Claude Code, Gemini, and Parallel.
- Existing Starter and Pro users must opt in to the new pricing, and the switch can't be undone. [...] Exa says Websets led the comparison on cost and result quality. The evidence remains narrow: Exa designed and ran the benchmarks, each category contains only 20 queries, and no independent evaluation is included. The results support a limited claim about those 40 prompts. Production evaluations should use representative queries and measure valid rows, missed entities, latency, and total cost.

## A metered bill replaces the subscription

New accounts now use consumption-based pricing. According to Exa's pricing reference, charges combine model computation, searches, and optional contact enrichment.

results.title: Websets V2: 4x Faster, 2x Cheaper | Exa Blog
results.content:
The harder the search, the smaller the savings. The Vanguard search reviewed 454 candidates to find 100 matches and cost 98% less than before. The climate tech search reviewed over 6,000 candidates, but only 19 met every criterion, so it cost about the same per match as legacy pricing.

Across Websets V2 searches, the cost per match is about half the legacy Pro price on average. That is an average, not a guarantee. Usage-based pricing charges for the work a search does, even when it finds few or no matches, so a very hard search can cost more per match than it did before.

Read more on V2’s new pricing here.

Websets V2 is available today. Try a complex search and build your next dataset. [...] Legacy plans charge a fixed 10 credits for every match, which is $0.045 per match on the Pro plan. Usage-based pricing charges for the compute and searches a Webset uses, so the cost per match depends on how hard your matches are to find. Here are four Websets V2 searches, from easiest to hardest.

| Search | Matches | Usage-based per match | Legacy Pro per match | V2 cost reduction |
------
| Investment professionals at Vanguard | 100 | $0.001 | $0.045 | 98% |
| Independent search engines | 100 | $0.006 | $0.045 | 87% |
| Semiconductor equity analysts at major investment firms | 100 | $0.012 | $0.045 | 74% |
| US climate tech startups whose founder published a paper since 2023 | 19 | $0.044 | $0.045 | 2% | [...] We’re introducing a new usage-based pricing model where you pay for compute and search volume, with searches at $5 per 1,000 requests. On average, users on the new plan will pay half as much as before. There is no monthly subscription fee. Everyone on the usage plan gets access to the Websets API.

All existing Websets users get V2’s speed and quality improvements automatically. To get the lower pricing, switch from your legacy Starter or Pro plan to usage-based pricing on the billing page. Staying on your existing plan keeps your existing pricing.
